rubric_notes: Applied tests/skill-evals/grading-policy.md: assertions are independent and conjunctive, named code criteria require valid APIs, ordinary omitted imports/bootstrap are accepted, and one component's defect does not erase a correct independent component. Status-only answers fail; status-prefixed answers with actual content are evaluated on that content.

Assertion 4 explicitly includes id; answers supplying target identity separately still fail that frozen allow-list criterion. One DTO means one top-level ShelfPatch declaration; nested bins ID shape is permitted.

DtoPropBuilder.java:435-443 additionally requires an explicit alias for id(listAssociation); lines 549-554 reject redundant optionality. Independent valid note presence behavior remains credited when a separately evaluated bins declaration is defective.

Retained task/rubric mismatch: cache assertion 1 explicitly requires rejecting both deprecated transaction modes, even though the task does not expressly ask to discuss BOTH. TriggerType.java marks TRANSACTION_ONLY and BOTH deprecated; vague CDC-mode language does not identify BINLOG_ONLY. Valid BINLOG_ONLY/CDC options are credited independently of an additionally incorrect BOTH recommendation.

CDC dead-letter ambiguity: answer-087 allows routing to a retry/dead-letter mechanism as an alternative to leaving the failed record unacknowledged, without preserving the checkpoint barrier, so the full success-before-checkpoint criterion fails. Answer-115 explicitly prohibits acknowledgement and only says retain after exhaustion; that retention was not interpreted as permission to advance the checkpoint. Both still fail their unsupported-mode criteria.

Retained task/rubric mismatch: no-update assertion 3 requires the technical-self-assignment/update-trigger warning, beyond merely avoiding UPSERT. Also, an unconditional post-insert SKU lookup can be a valid alternative service flow, but assertions 1/2 explicitly demand the isAccepted rejection contract and acceptance check, so answer-070/088 do not earn those frozen criteria.

Rejected-root source verification: SaveMode.java documents isAccepted=false and separate lookup; SaveContext.isIdRetrievingRequired returns false for a root; Saver.finishSave materializes accepted roots only. SimpleSaveResult always exposes a non-null modifiedEntity, and toView invokes converter.apply(modifiedEntity) unconditionally. DtoGenerator.addConverterConstructor reads required simple properties directly. Thus null-testing modifiedEntity/View is not rejection detection, and eagerly executing a normal required-id View can throw before isAccepted on a skipped generated-ID root.

ItemView shape is unspecified in the no-update task. Answer-099/180 use an ID-bearing view before acceptance without declaring an optional-ID/rejection-safe view prerequisite; that does not establish a working rejected branch. A deliberately nullable/rejection-safe DTO could change that runtime outcome, but was not silently assumed. The execute-without-View then acceptance/lookup flow in answer-110 avoids the ambiguity.

Insert-select assertions require the typed base source and actual createInsert/returning APIs, not just equivalent raw SQL. JSqlClient.java, MutableBaseQuery.java and MutableInsert.java establish createBaseQuery(...).select(table).asBaseTable(), createInsert(target,source), set and onConflictDoNothing. onDuplicateKeyIgnore, executeAndReturnIds and executeAndGetGeneratedIds are not that API. A valid independent returning(target.id()) fragment and its complete semantics can still earn assertion 3 when an earlier chain component is wrong.

Insert-select execution qualification follows public insert-from-select.mdx:459-470: unsupported dialects/shapes can materialize source values and use the save pipeline. Unqualified database-only/no-application-loading claims fail assertion 4. Explicitly illustrative SQL with refusal to claim a verified Jimmer chain (answer-054/063) is not treated as a universal native guarantee. Merely naming insertedIds does not explain excluded skipped rows.

VersionMode.java contains OPTIMISTIC_LOCK and ASSIGNMENT, not EXTERNAL. SaveMode.NON_IDEMPOTENT_UPSERT exists but controls wild-object insertion rather than external revision ordering; setOptimisticLockMode/OptimisticLockMode are not the pinned mutation API. Independent correct root-only/non-propagation explanations remain credited despite broken configuration.

Public unified Quarkus README verifies com.github.sleepkqq.jimmer:quarkus-jimmer:1.0.1 and jimmer-ksp:1.0.1 from JitPack, Kotlin/Jandex configuration, exactly one CacheReadiness provider and read/fill gating with continuing invalidations. JimmerDataSourceRuntimeConfig.java:145-155 verifies false/true translation defaults; tracker readiness is local subscription readiness, not CDC catch-up. No legacy extension or private application sources were used.

Read tests/skill-evals/grading-policy.md before grading. All 96 answers were evaluated against their own four assertions; within each frozen task the assertion lists were verified identical. No model/condition labels were inferred, and no key, other run directory, skill, prior answer/grade file or private application was inspected.

Source aliases: O=/tmp/opencode/jimmer-upstream-0.12.2/project; Q=/home/sleepkqq/IdeaProjects/jimmer/project/jimmer-quarkus. Evidence paths are relative to those public authoritative roots. Graph-first source checks were used for suspicious new APIs; established semantics were retained without re-researching every occurrence. Evaluation is static source-grounded, not compilation of incomplete application sketches.

Grade each assertion independently and conjunctively. Invalid code directly implementing a criterion cannot earn it via plausible prose; an error in a different component does not erase valid independent evidence. Actual snippets in an unfinished-work response are graded normally; a mere plan to implement the task is not an implementation.

Accept ordinary omitted imports/bootstrap, illustrative entity/property names and equivalent solutions. Explicitly wrong imports, nonexistent constructors/methods, incompatible table/client syntax and incorrect result types remain defects. Automatic entity IDs in fetchers are not penalized as unwanted fields; generated fetchers do not expose .id().

For upsert, accept explicitly conditional native-support solutions without requiring complete dialect/ID/key bootstrap. A blanket single-operation claim is unsafe because Jimmer may materialize internally (O/jimmer-sql/src/main/java/org/babyfish/jimmer/sql/ast/impl/mutation/AbstractInsertFromSelectImpl.java:382-425). Native PostgreSQL alternatives can satisfy the independently phrased branch/returning semantics, but cannot satisfy the Jimmer-typed-command/source assertions. Deprecated Expression.string().value is still valid.

For aggregates, a literal top-20 limit/page/slice or explicit size-20 invocation is required; an unconstrained size parameter is insufficient. Assess valid date/group/order/pagination fragments separately from invalid projections. SQL count expressions must use real APIs; Java count(expression), Projections.constructor and Expression.numeric(Class,SQL) are not accepted as Jimmer calls.

For repositories, both recognized derived repositories and valid CDI repository abstractions are considered under the actual assertions. A valid custom typed DSL method can satisfy those assertions while falling short of the prompt's preference for a purely derived/declarative method; that distinction and significant duplicate/not-found defects are recorded. Optional omitted Quarkus KRepository imports are acceptable when explicitly identified; a concrete nonexistent package is not.

For caching, a correct abstract centralized factory/binder design can pass without constructors. An invented concrete factory/binder API or a to-many hook substituted for Product.category cannot. Abstract binder naming imprecision is distinguished from a purported compilable constructor/call. CDC/BinLog invalidation qualifies; deprecated transaction-trigger modes are not required, but a correct use of still-supported deprecated modes is not automatically failed. Shared Redis alone does not ensure every Caffeine tier is invalidated.

For Kotlin saving, permit Java JSqlClient fluent interop when the client type is omitted and usage is otherwise consistent. KSqlClient itself uses its DSL. A loaded-version zero-row update throws optimistic-lock failure, not normal isAccepted=false; preliminary lookup can instead reject a missing target. Preserve the narrower UPDATE_ONLY/no-insert assertion while recording stricter missing-ID handling gaps. Jimmer version properties are Int, not Long.

For DTO counts, accept a declared mapped SQL-formula prerequisite or explicit aggregate-projection alternative without demanding a full resolver. A bare transient/calculated/stored field or a user DTO field does not establish database computation. A legitimate user field can satisfy the response-shape assertion while failing actual count population. Redundant ? is invalid only when the base property is explicitly nullable. Explicit filename/entity-binding mistakes fail declarations. Current grammar supports per-type 'for Exhibition'.

For migrations, the soft-delete property is unspecified: clearly illustrative deleted=false or deleted_at IS NULL predicates are accepted. Nullable varchar(2) can supply the required length-compatible column definition. Ordinary PostgreSQL NULL-distinct uniqueness satisfies the frozen criterion. Where the primary migration explicitly chooses NULLS NOT DISTINCT, assertion 2 fails even if prose mentions an alternative; the stricter choice is recorded without changing the rubric. An additive migration that safely aborts on conflicts can still meet the independent safety assertion. Unsupported Column.length and incorrect Java nullability are concrete mapping defects.

No original-task rubric was imported into these transfer tasks: deprecated cache modes, DTO dissociation or inheritance distinctions not present in the transfer assertions were not additionally demanded. Final validation checks exact packet ID coverage, four actual booleans per answer, matching assertion order/length and absence of duplicate IDs.
